title: Rate limits and metering design review
summary: Design review for launch rate limiting and metering. The team locked D-12: a per-tenant token bucket in the gateway Redis with an enterprise burst of 3,000 requests per second for 60 seconds, which satisfies Acme's R-12, and D-13: every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset headers per R-14. Metering stays asynchronous per D-09 and K-04.
utterances: Okay, launch is six weeks out. Finance wants per-tenant rate limits and metering live on day one. Priya, where are we?
Proposal is a token bucket per tenant, counters in the Redis cluster that already sits next to Envoy, so no new hop on the request path.
What do the tiers look like? Standard 500 sustained, enterprise 1,000, like D-10 says?
Yes. The open part is burst. Acme's nightly sync hits 3,000 a second for about a minute.
That's R-12, it's in their contract. If we cap enterprise burst at 2,000 we throttle our launch customer on night one.
Could we just give Acme a custom override and keep the tier at 2,000?
We could, but Globex and Initech will have similar batch jobs. I'd rather the enterprise tier itself allows 3,000 for 60 seconds.
Agreed. So: enterprise burst 3,000 per second for 60 seconds, bucket in gateway Redis.
On metering: we do not touch billing Postgres from the gateway. K-04, it fell over at 3,000 writes a second.
Right, gateway publishes to usage.events and the metering consumer rolls up hourly. That's D-09 and D-03, nothing new.
Acme also asked to see remaining quota. Can we put that in headers?
X-RateLimit-Limit, Remaining and Reset on every response, read straight from the bucket. Costs nothing.
Let's lock that too: rate limit headers on every response.

locks.text: Per-tenant token bucket in the gateway Redis: standard 500 req/s and enterprise 1,000 req/s sustained, enterprise burst up to 3,000 req/s for 60 s (satisfies Acme's R-12); no new hop on the request path.
Every public API response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers read from the tenant's bucket (satisfies R-14).
